newsitem.title: USA: Senate panel to vote on US Housing Secy on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Senate panel to vote on US Housing Secy on Tuesday.

text.p: The Senate Banking Committee will vote on the nomination of Andrew Cuomo as Housing Secretary next Tuesday, committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato said.
"It is my intent to have the committee act as expeditiously as possible," the New York Republican said after a three-hour hearing Wednesday on Cuomo's nomination.
If the committee approves Cuomo's nomination, D'Amato said he hoped the full Senate would vote on it also next week.
President Clinton named Cuomo to replace Henry Cisneros as head of the Department of Housing and Urban Development.

"Assuming favorably, and I would think probably unanimous committee action," D'Amato said he hoped the Senate leadership would agree to "expedite floor action so we can move this to the floor next week."
Senators grilled Cuomo, who is a HUD assistant secretary and son of former New York Governor Mario Cuomo, about problems they saw at the housing agency.
The main concerns expressed by senators were that HUD was too big and unwieldy to operate efficiently and also over the "Section 8" government subsidized housing program.
Many contracts that the government has with property owners of Section 8 housing are expiring over the next few years and the renewal of those contracts have a cost attached.

D'Amato displayed a chart at the hearing that showed assistance for the renewal of expiring Section 8 contracts would jump to $10.2 billion in fiscal 1998, which starts in October, from $3.6 billion in fiscal 1997. HUD's whole budget for fiscal 1997 was $19.5 billion.
"HUD faces a fiscal crisis. Hard choices must be made regarding discretionary spending priorities," said D'Amato, who supports Cuomo's nomination.
Cuomo, 39, said he was committed to reducing the number of HUD personnel by the year 2000 to 7,500 from 10,400 now.
Sen. Lauch Faircloth, R-N.C., who has introduced legislation in the past to abolish HUD, said the agency had become a "massive" bureaucracy that had lost the ability to manage itself.
Cuomo said during the hearing that he was committed to improving management and financial accountability of HUD.
"It will be my top priority period. I will continue to build on Secretary Cisneros's efforts," he told the senators.
